S7020T Terminal Insertion Machine — AC clips and terminals inserted without a single hand

Two servo-driven insertion heads place terminals, AC clips and spring clips from reel or bowl feeders at up to 12,000 CPH — with vision-guided programming that replaces the whole manual insertion bench.
Part of the unified S7020 platform: switch feeder and gripper to move between terminal, eyelet, pin and tact-switch insertion. Final configuration confirmed after technical review.

blocks.heading: The clip bench is where your line slows down and quality leaks

nodes.text: The hidden cost of manual clip insertion
The clip bench is where your line slows down and quality leaks
AC clips and terminals are small, springy and polarized. Inserted by hand, they consume headcount and fail in ways you only find at test.
Clip insertion is pure handwork
AC clips and terminals are pressed in one at a time. It is a bench of operators, not a process — and it scales only with headcount.
Crooked, floating and missed clips
Manual press force varies operator to operator. Tilted clips and shallow seats pass visual checks and fail at wave or final test.
Polarity and position errors
Clips have an orientation. Hand insertion mixes them up quietly, and the mistake surfaces only downstream — where rework is most expensive.
Turnover resets the skill curve
Clip insertion feel takes weeks to learn. Every seasonal worker or new hire restarts the defect curve from zero.
The line balances around the bench
SMT runs at machine speed, then boards queue at the manual terminal station. The bench — not the mounter — sets your output.
Labor cost compounds
Every volume increase means more seats at the clip bench. Wages rise, availability falls, and the cost per board climbs with them.

Technical evaluation FAQ
Questions buyers ask before ordering

nodes.q: What components can the S7020T insert?
nodes.a: Terminals, AC clips and hardware spring clips in bulk or reel packaging, with terminal thickness from 0.5 to 1.2 mm. The insertion hole should be 0.5 ± 0.1 mm larger than the component lead, and components keep a minimum 2 mm distance. Typical applications are chargers, power adapters, automotive electronics, small appliances and 5G boards.

nodes.q: How fast is it compared with manual insertion?
nodes.a: The S7020T inserts at 12,000 CPH with two heads. A manual operator typically places a few hundred clips per hour, so one machine replaces at least five to ten inserters — that is the ROI case in one line.

nodes.q: Can it feed both bulk and reel-packed terminals?
nodes.a: Yes. The feeding system supports vibration bowl feeders for bulk terminals and reel feeders for taped components, so both packaging formats run on the same machine.

nodes.q: How is a new board programmed?
nodes.a: Through online visual programming with visual correction, plus EXCEL import and USB data input. Teaching a new board takes minutes rather than hours, which keeps high-mix clip production economical.

Yes. The production reference platform uses a guide-rail automatic conveyor with left-to-right board flow for inline production; standalone operation is also available. Board sizes up to 410×360 mm are supported on the inline platform, and enlarged sizes can be customized.
